about: Shared rules fixtures for clients that reimplement Ember Core's day rules without a server (web/src/lib/local/). Generated from Core by tests/Ember.Tests/RulesFixtureTests.cs, which fails when Core and this file disagree; after a deliberate rule change, regenerate the expected values with EMBER_WRITE_FIXTURES=1 dotnet test --filter RulesFixtureTests (inputs are kept, expected is rewritten). Each case: name, today (the user's local day), from (first day of the expected days and dayStats ranges, which run through today), timezone, graceDaysPerWeek, lowDays (the user's low days), habits, routines and expected. A habit: id, frequency (daily|weekly|weekdays), weeklyTarget (weekly only, else null), days (weekdays only: mon..sun, else null), timesPerDay, startDate (the habit was created at 12:00 UTC on this day), pausedFrom and pausedUntil (inclusive pause range; pausedFrom null with pausedUntil set pauses every day up to pausedUntil), routineId, and logs { date, count, completed } where completed is the stored done flag: set when count reached timesPerDay at the time of the check-in, so a day stays done after the target rises (only today is recomputed on a target change, and past days whose count reaches a lowered target become done, with counts above it clamped to it). A routine: id and habitIds in routine order. expected.days[habitId]: one { date, state, completed, count } per day from..today; state is the first that applies of beforestart, paused, lowday, done, partial, offday, pending (today or yesterday), notdone; completed is the log's flag (null without a log or when partial). expected.stats[habitId]: exactly the API Habit DTO stats { streak, graceUsed, bestStreak, last7, week }: weekly habits have streak, graceUsed and bestStreak null and week { done, target }; other habits week null. expected.dayStats: one { date, scheduled, done, partial, showedUp } per day from..today. expected.routinePending[routineId]: ids of the member habits a routine reminder today lists (pending or partial today), in routine order. expected.weekly: what GET /api/stats/weekly returns on today (the 7 days ending yesterday): { totalDone, totalPossible, headline, footer, habits [{ habitId, name, done, possible, streak }] } in English with Discord markdown stripped; habit names are "Habit {id}", streak is null for weekly habits, and headline and footer are empty when totalPossible is 0. A weekly habit with weeklyTarget null uses the default target 3 in stats.week and expected.weekly. edits: single-habit edits run through Core's HabitService on edits.today (UTC), on a daily habit created on 2027-01-01 at 12:00 UTC (habit id 1 on the client side). edits.pause: { name, pausedFrom, pausedUntil (the habit before), until (POST /api/habits/{id}/pause; null resumes), expected { pausedFrom, pausedUntil } }. edits.writeDay: { name, timesPerDay, date, log (the day's log before, or null), edit ({ completed: true|false } checks in done or not done, { completed: null } clears the day, { count } sets the count), expected (the day's log after, or null) }. edits.retarget: { name, timesPerDay, newTimesPerDay (the schedule change), logs (before), expected (logs after, by date) }. limits.local: the limits web/src/lib/local/limits.ts enforces like the API (all of them except rangeDays, an API constant Core doesn't hold), from Core constants and the database model's column lengths; limits.fireside: web/src/lib/fireside-limits.ts, from FiresideService. Core also treats an unlogged day on its timezone switchover date (2026-10-11) as protected in streaks; the fixtures use 2027 dates and avoid it.

pause.name: extending a running pause keeps its start
pausing after an ended pause starts a new one today
pausing before a planned pause starts it today
resuming a running pause ends it yesterday
resuming a pause that started today removes it
resuming after a pause ended keeps the past pause
resuming a pause without a start ends it yesterday
resuming a planned pause removes it
resuming when not paused changes nothing

writeDay.name: done on a new day logs the full count
done on a three times a day habit
not done over a done day
clearing a day without a log
a count below the target is partial
a count at the target is done
lowering the count of a done day
a day done before the target rose stays done at the same count
a day done before the target rose stays done when more are logged
a day done before the target rose is not done below its count
a count of zero is not done

retarget.name: raising the target recomputes only today
lowering the target makes days that reach it done
lowering the target clamps counts above it and makes those days done
lowering the target to one clamps every count
